content: 1. Monitor patients for withdrawal symptoms when transitioning to buprenorphine long-acting injection, especially if co-administered with CYP3A4 inhibitors like atazanavir. Atazanavir increases buprenorphine levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy or monitor closely. 2. If signs of buprenorphine toxicity or overdose occur within two weeks and the CYP3A4 inhibitor cannot be reduced or discontinued, transition the patient back to a buprenorphine formulation that allows dose adjustments. 3. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of buspirone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 4. Atazanavir increases cabazitaxel levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing toxicity. Avoid co-administration or modify therapy and monitor closely. 5. Atazanavir affects calcifediol metabolism by inhibiting CYP3A4, CYP24A1, and CYP27B1 enzymes, potentially altering serum vitamin D levels and reducing calcitriol conversion. Dose adjustment of calcifediol may be required, and serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D, intact PTH, and calcium levels should be monitored closely when initiating or discontinuing strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 6. Atazanavir increases cannabidiol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Consider reducing the cannabidiol dose when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor therapy closely. 7. Atazanavir increases capmatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 8. Atazanavir increases carbamazepine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor plasma levels when used concomitantly. 9. Atazanavir increases cariprazine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors requires cariprazine dose reduction. Refer to the dosage modification section in the drug monograph. 10. Atazanavir enhances carvedilol effects through pharmacodynamic synergy, increasing the risk of hypotension, bradycardia, AV block, and prolonged PR interval. Consider lowering the beta-blocker dose and monitor therapy closely. 11. Cenobamate decreases atazanavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Increase the dose of CYP3A4 substrates as needed when co-administered with cenobamate. Monitor therapy closely. 12. Ceritinib increases atazanavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 13. Atazanavir increases chlordiazepoxide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing toxicity. Use alternatives if available or consider lowering the benzodiazepine dose. Monitor therapy closely. 14. Atazanavir increases inhaled ciclesonide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, increasing the risk of Cushing's syndrome or adrenal suppression. Use caution and monitor therapy. 15. Atazanavir increases cilostazol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 16. Cimetidine increases atazanavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 17. Atazanavir increases cinacalcet levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 18. Atazanavir increases citalopram levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 19. Clarithromycin increases atazanavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 20. Atazanavir increases clomipramine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 21. Atazanavir increases clonazepam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing toxicity. Use alternatives if available or consider lowering the benzodiazepine dose. Monitor therapy closely. 22. Atazanavir decreases clopidogrel levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, reducing clopidogrel bioactivation. Use caution and monitor therapy. 23. Atazanavir increases clorazepate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing toxicity. Use alternatives if available or consider lowering the benzodiazepine dose. Monitor therapy closely. 24. Atazanavir increases clozapine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 25. Atazanavir may increase or decrease conjugated estrogens levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use alternatives if available or monitor therapy closely. 26. Atazanavir increases cortisone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 27. Atazanavir increases crizotinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 28. Crofelemer increases atazanavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism in the gut. Systemic inhibition is unlikely due to minimal absorption. Use caution and monitor therapy. 29. Atazanavir increases cyclophosphamide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing toxicity. Use caution and monitor therapy. 30. Atazanavir increases cyclosporine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 31. Dabrafenib decreases atazanavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 32. Danazol increases atazanavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 33. Danicopan increases atazanavir levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Consider dose reduction of P-gp substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious adverse reactions. Use caution and monitor therapy. 34. Atazanavir increases darifenacin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 35. Atazanavir increases darunavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor therapy. 36. Atazanavir increases dasatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 37. Deferasirox decreases atazanavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 38. Atazanavir increases deflazacort levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Decrease the deflazacort dose to one-third of the recommended dose if co-administered with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor therapy closely. 39. Atazanavir increases desipramine levels through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 40. Atazanavir may increase or decrease desogestrel levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use alternatives if available or monitor therapy closely. 41. Atazanavir increases desvenlafaxine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing toxicity. Use caution and monitor therapy. 42. Atazanavir increases dexamethasone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 43. Atazanavir increases diazepam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing toxicity. Use alternatives if available or consider lowering the benzodiazepine dose. Monitor therapy closely. 44. Atazanavir increases diazepam buccal levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing adverse reactions. Use caution and monitor therapy. 45. Atazanavir increases diazepam intranasal levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing adverse reactions. Use caution and monitor therapy. 46. Atazanavir increases diazoxide effects, potentially causing hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance associated with protease inhibitors. Use caution and monitor therapy. 47. Atazanavir increases diclofenac levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing toxicity. Use caution and monitor therapy. 48. Didanosine decreases atazanavir levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor therapy. 49. Atazanavir may increase or decrease dienogest/estradiol valerate levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use alternatives if available or monitor therapy closely. 50. Atazanavir enhances digoxin effects through pharmacodynamic synergy, increasing the risk of AV block. Use caution and monitor therapy. 51. Atazanavir increases diltiazem levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially causing toxicities such as hypotension and AV block. Reduce the diltiazem dose by 50%, monitor blood pressure, and perform ECG monitoring. 52. Atazanavir increases dofetilide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, increasing the risk of QT prolongation and cardiac arrhythmias. Use alternatives if available or monitor therapy closely. 53. Atazanavir increases dolasetron levels, increasing the risk of cardiac arrhythmias. Use alternatives if available or monitor therapy closely. 54. Atazanavir increases doravirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing plasma concentrations and toxicities. Use caution and monitor therapy. 55. Atazanavir increases dosulepin levels through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 56. Atazanavir increases doxepin levels through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 57. Atazanavir increases doxorubicin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 58. Atazanavir increases doxorubicin liposomal levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 59. Atazanavir increases dronabinol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 60. Atazanavir may increase or decrease drospirenone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use alternatives if available or monitor therapy closely. 61. Atazanavir increases duvelisib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, increasing the risk of duvelisib toxicities. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 62. Duvelisib increases atazanavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 63. Atazanavir increases elagolix levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration of elagolix 200 mg BID with strong CYP3A inhibitors for more than one month is not recommended. Monitor therapy closely. 64. Elagolix decreases atazanavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor CYP3A substrates if co-administered and consider increasing the CYP3A substrate dose if needed. 65. Atazanavir increases eletriptan levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 66. Atazanavir increases eltrombopag levels by decreasing metabolism through UGT inhibition. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear. Use caution and monitor therapy. 67. Atazanavir increases elvitegravir levels significantly. There are no data to alter current dosing recommendations. The recommended dose is elvitegravir 85 mg PO once daily with atazanavir/ritonavir other than 300/100 mg once daily. Use caution and monitor therapy. 68. Atazanavir increases elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 69. Atazanavir and emtricitabine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor therapy. 70. Atazanavir and encorafenib interact through CYP3A4 metabolism. Encorafenib both inhibits and induces CYP3A4 at clinically relevant plasma concentrations. Use caution and monitor therapy.
